profile_text.body:
HeyGen is a Los Angeles-based company that provides an AI video generation platform. The site describes the platform as accepting text, image, or audio as input and producing complete videos with narration, captions, visuals, and animations. It is built on a five-stage AI training pipeline that the company says captures how a person looks, moves, gestures, and expresses themselves. Features include AI avatars, voice cloning, lip-synced video translation across more than 175 languages and dialects, a text-based editor for controlling tone and delivery, and tools the company calls Voice Director, Voice Mirroring, Gesture Control, and Realistic Previews. The platform also converts PowerPoint and PDF files into narrated video scenes, and can turn audio recordings such as podcasts into avatar-driven video. HeyGen additionally offers HyperFrames, described as an open-source video rendering framework that lets AI agents create videos using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, and has integrated Seedance 2.0 for what the company calls cinematic AI video generation and realistic digital twins.

The company describes itself as having more than 30 million users, customers across 196 countries, and adoption across 85 percent of the Fortune 100. It offers a free plan alongside paid tiers with additional capabilities.

The site's held facts list HeyGen's core product under the Video Generation and Editing category, with a noted concern around likeness and consent risk. No litigation, MCP server registrations, SEC filings, or patent records are present in the available data.
